transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's hard to explain, but it's especially bad when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle things like paperwork, or when I need to sit down and go over shared household plans. I just can't seem to settle down and do it.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty settling down and staying focused on tasks like paperwork?
It's been noticeably worse for about a year and five months now. That's when I got married, and we started having to merge our routines and handle a lot more of that kind of stuff together.
Before you got married about a year and a half ago, did you ever have trouble sitting still or focusing on tasks like reading, paperwork, or other activities that required you to stay in one place?

Yeah, um... looking back, this was actually already a part of me way back in elementary school. It's not just a recent thing. I was always the girl with a completely messy desk, and I was constantly forgetting my permission slips. My parents were always getting notes from my teachers saying that I talked out of turn, or that I just seemed unable to stay seated during class. So, yes, it's definitely been there for a long time.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F91.9 (conduct disorder - no behavioral rule violations mentioned), F93.0 (separation anxiety - not applicable), F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder - symptoms predate marriage stressor and are consistent with ADHD rather than anxiety), and F32.9 (depression - no depressive symptoms reported). Patient presents with lifelong history of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity dating to elementary school, which is pathognomonic for ADHD. Symptoms worsened with marriage due to increased demands for sustained attention and organization, but core presentation is ADHD.
